question: Does a reduced parameterization remove inactive/confounded degrees of freedom, and does continuous task calibration improve concentration and screening on new constant conditions?
claim_C1: Reparameterization removes the N-removal scale gauge relative to NH4/DO observations when the oxygen coefficient is also free; it does not identify physical constants or preserve SNO under arbitrary gauge changes.
claim_C2: The continuous full model is compared with continuous regression using identical 750 target values; any superiority is to be assessed after freeze, not assumed.
claim_C3: Fixed-ratio full versus no-feedback is the matched five-parameter ablation; the six-parameter calibrated version has additional flexibility and is not that causal pair.
cap_basis: On development domain L<=1,T>=2,f<=0.1,steady N removal <=(40.5+0.1*312)/2=35.85<40. The cap is inactive there by construction; transient activation is separately monitored.
historical_prior: All process models retain the original empirical biomass closure. Pure regressors use L,z only, so matching target supervision does not eliminate all historical prior/capacity differences.
limitations: Six new conditions do not establish general risk or plant validity.
Continuous calibration is a new study version, not retroactive repair of M1/M2.
Profile loss and Jacobian rank are diagnostics, not physical parameter confidence intervals.
No temperature/dynamic extension or measured plant energy is claimed.
All failed/negative results and all pre-reference predictions are retained.
authorization: User requested code modifications and autonomous local execution, including Python/PyTorch as needed. NumPy/SciPy/Numba suffice for this small model.
outputs: prospective freeze and raw new BSM1 references
independent raw audit and versioned Chinese report
